name: Experimental design
proof: I designed and ran six studies for my dissertation, with plans registered in advance, and recruited more than 3,000 people. My master's thesis was an experiment with 305 participants, also registered in advance.

name: Longitudinal and repeated-measures design
proof: I ran a 15-day behavior-change study (560 recruited, 455 retained) and managed seven-day student diary studies, with about four surveys a day.

name: Causal and quasi-experimental methods
proof: I used matching, regression discontinuity and difference-in-differences on records for more than 100,000 students.

name: Crossover trial analysis
also: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial
proof: I am first author on a 2026 analysis of a randomized, double-blind crossover trial of a ghrelin-receptor blocker in 29 people with alcohol use disorder. The NIH team designed the trial. I ran the analysis.

name: Mixed-methods program evaluation
proof: I evaluated a university summer-skills program with focus groups, surveys and student outcome data, then presented what worked to department leaders.

name: Research synthesis
proof: I wrote literature reviews on smartphone use and on COVID-19 social contact, and pooled the raw data from eight experiments.

name: Open and reproducible research
proof: I write my analysis plan down and register it publicly before I look at results. I share code and materials, and I co-founded a campus open-science group.

name: Survey and questionnaire development
proof: I built the surveys for every study I have run, programmed them in Qualtrics, and wrote items for a published gaming-motivation scale.

name: Scale development and psychometrics
proof: I built the trust measures for my dissertation and a smartphone self-inclusion scale (in preparation, first author). I also contributed to a published gaming scale and a VR symptom questionnaire.

name: Participant recruitment
proof: I recruit in person, through university pools, and on MTurk, CloudResearch and Prolific. I also handle recruitment administration for an NIH clinical trial.

name: Online-panel data quality
proof: I screen out inattentive and duplicate respondents. In a COVID-19 survey, 674 people consented and 569 passed.

name: Behavioral intervention measurement
proof: I designed dissertation Study 6, which tracked trust, adherence and behavior for 15 days. It found no reliable effect, and I reported it that way.

name: Content and media coding
proof: I coded video for prejudice in media, transcribed focus groups, and analyzed emotional speech in earlier lab roles.

name: Regression and multilevel modeling
proof: I fit linear, logistic, ordinal, negative-binomial and mixed-effects models. I pooled eight experiments (1,778 people) into one multilevel model.

name: Mediation and moderation
proof: I tested who is affected and why: a multilevel mediated-moderation model in my dissertation, and causal mediation in the generative AI experiments.

name: Structural equation modeling
proof: I built latent-variable path models for an award-winning data competition entry, replicated a published model in R for a graduate course, and ran Mplus models for my dissertation.

name: Power and sensitivity analysis
proof: I plan sample sizes before each study and check what each one can detect. I taught a power-analysis workshop in 2023.

name: Robustness checks
proof: In the generative AI study I tested the main result 69 ways, so the conclusion does not rest on one analysis choice.

name: Cross-study data integration
proof: I pooled eight experiments for a published analysis. Along the way I found and removed 173 placeholder rows.

name: Data cleaning and quality control
proof: I prepared the data for the parasocial study, the pooled analysis, and more than 100,000 student records.

name: Data visualization and dashboards
proof: I built Tableau dashboards that department chairs and administrators used each semester, and the figures for the generative AI study.

name: Bayesian inference
proof: I use Bayes factors to show how strongly the data support a null result, including on the Studies 1 and 2 pages of this site. I have not built full Bayesian models.

name: Latent profile analysis
proof: I completed a 2023 methods workshop. My first applied project is still ahead.

name: Machine learning and prediction
proof: I built and tested classifiers in an end-to-end Python project for a graduate course, and presented a poster predicting app use. I have not deployed a model.

name: R, Stata and SPSS
proof: R is my main language for modeling, figures and teaching. I used Stata across a graduate sequence in regression and program evaluation.

name: Cloud and API experiment engineering
proof: I built a participant-facing task on the ChatGPT API, hosted on AWS, with random assignment in Qualtrics. It is a research tool, not production software.

name: Text analysis with dictionaries
proof: I ran LIWC text analysis at a university lab in 2018 and 2019, and compared human and AI writing with similarity scores in the generative AI study.

name: Modern text analysis
proof: I took a 2023 text-analytics workshop and a graduate course on TF-IDF and language processing. My first applied project is still ahead.

name: Python
proof: I used pandas, Jupyter, web scraping and scikit-learn in graduate coursework. R is the language I use daily.

name: SQL
proof: I am building SQL skills through self-directed practice and have not used it in a project yet.

name: Geospatial analysis
proof: I mapped open Los Angeles County data in ArcGIS for a 2018 data competition entry.

name: Human-AI trust and reliance research
proof: My six-study dissertation compares trust in doctors and medical AI. It measures reliance by how far people move their own answer toward the advice.

name: Human-AI collaboration experiments
proof: I am co-first author on two experiments (N = 1,299) on drafting with generative AI versus editing its output. Judges who did not know the condition rated the work.

name: Obedience to computer authority
proof: My master's thesis (N = 305) tested whether people obey computer instructors as readily as human ones. They did, about equally, and I reported that as a null.

name: Health and risk communication research
proof: I study how people read genetic-risk information. On a virtual-patient project (N = 200) I collected, cleaned and analyzed the data.

name: Research program management
proof: I managed six to seven projects at once at Georgetown with a student team, and I now support six NIH projects.

name: Supervising and mentoring
proof: I have supervised research assistants since 2017, on teams of up to 15. I guided an honors thesis and served as a conference graduate mentor.

name: Research governance
proof: I wrote and managed ethics-board protocols at two universities and support regulated clinical-study administration at NIH.

name: Workflow and process improvement
proof: I redesigned the Georgetown participant pool, and research yield reportedly rose 50% the next year. I also built reusable lab templates.

name: Grants and budgets
proof: I won three named grants and fellowships, and I wrote the budgets and timelines for my funded and independent research.

name: Policy work
proof: I served on the task force whose recommendation on storing and showing gender identity and pronouns became policy. I also sat on the committee behind making the GRE optional at Georgetown.

name: Curriculum and course design
proof: I designed and taught Psychology of Technology as instructor of record. It won Georgetown's 2023 Graduate Student Teaching Award.

name: Workshop design and facilitation
proof: I taught workshops on power analysis, R and open science, then Introduction to R and Quarto at NIH.

name: Scientific writing
proof: I wrote all of my thesis and dissertation, and I contributed writing to several papers.

name: Talks and public communication
proof: I chaired a 2024 conference session on AI, and gave invited talks at the University of Virginia and a film festival.
